assertions.text: Output contains at least one markdown table (using | column | syntax)
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Weekday Hours | Sunday Hours | Holiday Hours...

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Pay?', 'Rate?')
assertions.evidence: Total Pay? column header present in Weekly Pay Calculation table

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns or conditions ('Part-time weekday', 'Full week with overtime', 'Sunday shift') — not outcomes ('Gets overtime', 'Double pay').
assertions.evidence: Scenarios like 'Regular weekday hours under limit', 'One hour over threshold', 'Weekday regular + Sunday' describe conditions, not outcomes

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Weekday hours', 'Sunday hours', 'Hourly rate', 'Weekly pay?') — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Weekday Hours, Sunday Hours, Holiday Hours, Hourly Rate, Overtime Threshold, Total Pay?

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Weekday Hours | Sunday Hours - Scenario is first column

assertions.text: The overtime threshold boundary (40 hours) is covered with at least a value at the threshold and one above.
assertions.evidence: 'Weekday hours exactly at threshold' row has 40 hours; 'One hour over threshold' has 41 hours

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Weekly Pay Calculation table mixes rate classification (determining 1x/1.5x/2x multipliers) and arithmetic verification (hours × rate calculation) in a single table rather than separating these distinct testing concerns

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Weekly Pay Calculation has 13 rows mixing rate selection scenarios (e.g., 'Sunday hours only', 'Holiday hours only') with arithmetic scenarios, indicating rows for multiple concerns combined rather than each isolated

assertions.text: Payable hours categorisation (1x regular, 1.5x overtime, 2x Sunday/holiday) and pay calculation (hours × rate) are in separate tables
assertions.evidence: Rate classification note ('1× ($10), 1.5× ($15), 2× ($20)') appears only as explanatory text; no dedicated table validates rate selection rules separately from the single Weekly Pay Calculation table that performs both classification and arithmetic
